_doc: Mary-O's own half of `asset editor-art`: the nouns this game invented, and
the engine art they should wear in the LDtk editor. Everything shared with
the rest of Ambition (Solid, OneWayPlatform, PickupSpawn, the IntGrid
values) is mapped by the tool itself — this file only says what the tool
A bare name is an engine entity sprite (assets/sprites/entities/<name>.png);
anything with a slash is a path under the sprite folder; and
{sheet, animation, frame} is one frame of a generated sheet, which is how
you name a CHARACTER or a construction prop. Re-run after editing:
_entity_art_doc: ⛔ pipes come from the SHEET, not from assets/sprites/props/mary_o_pipe_*.png.
Those files are a July leftover under a name nothing loads any more, and they
are still the old GREEN pipe — which is why the editor showed a green pipe
months after the game turned copper. `super_mary_o_pipe_top` is the target
_field_art_doc: Art that follows a FIELD, per placed instance. LDtk can only vary an
entity's tile by an ENUM value, so the field has to be one — either declared
in mary_o.entities.json (a noun this game owns, like MaryOBlock.kind) or
here via `enum` + `values` (an ENGINE def no per-world manifest declares,
Closing a field is refused if the level already authors a value the enum
does not spell — the tool names it rather than dropping it.
_field_display_doc: Fields the EDITOR should say out loud. A block's look deliberately never
announces its contents — that is the game's rule and it stays — but an
author is not a player, and the editor is where you need to see which brick
